title.rendered: A Statement

excerpt.rendered: Following today’s (18 August) statement from Cataclean, TOCA confirms the...

content.rendered:
Following today’s (18 August) statement from Cataclean, TOCA confirms the team will continue competing in the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship under a new name and management structure, in order that it can move positively forward.

The matters concerned are internal to the organisation and relate solely to its directors, shareholders and relevant parties. TOCA is not privy to those matters.

However, TOCA has been provided with assurances of the team’s participation in the BTCC going forward. Those assurances reflect Cataclean’s continuing commitment and confidence in both the team and the Championship.

We understand that the programme will operate through a new entity, without the further involvement of Jason Plato in its management or ownership.

In the interim, the team will be entered as CPRL.

Jason is unquestionably one of the BTCC’s greatest stars, and his exceptional record speaks for itself. He has long been – and will remain – a valued part of the BTCC family. Although his involvement with this particular venture appears to have reached its conclusion, we look forward to seeing Jason in the BTCC paddock in the future.

title.rendered: Donington Park GP awaits Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport

excerpt.rendered: Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport head to Donington Park...

content.rendered:
Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport head to Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August) for event seven of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, returning to the venue for a second time this season, this time on the longer GP configuration.

The squad arrives on the back of a front-row start, podium finish and an Independent victory at Knockhill, where home hero Gordon Shedden claimed the 142nd rostrum of his career and team-mate Árón Taylor-Smith banked a solid points haul in Fife. The aim now is to carry that momentum back to the scene of the season opener.

At 2.49 miles, the GP layout adds a further test for the drivers and opens up more genuine overtaking opportunities, with the addition of the Melbourne Hairpin.

Both drivers have form at the extended layout. Dubliner Taylor-Smith swept to a hat-trick of Independent class wins on the GP circuit in 2024, in addition to a hard-fought overall second place in 2023. Shedden, meanwhile, has eight victories at the Leicestershire venue, with his outing on the GP circuit last year rewarding him with a third-place finish.

Heading into round seven, Shedden occupies tenth in the Drivers' Championship, with Taylor-Smith occupying 14th. Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport sit sixth in the Teams' Championship and third in the Independent Teams' Championship, with the team focused on closing the gap in both standings as the second half of the season continues.

Following Saturday morning's opening 50-minute Free Practice session (11:00), the all-important Qualifying session (14:05) and 9-lap Qualifying Race (15:05) will determine the grid for Sunday's three races.

Sunday's races are scheduled for 11:45, 14:45 and 17:30 (BST), with all three broadcast live on ITV4 and ITVX in the UK, Racer Network in North America, and the BTCC YouTube channel everywhere else in the world.

Árón Taylor-Smith (#50) said: "Donington GP is a circuit that holds plenty of good memories for me, with the likes of my return to the podium in 2023 after seven years away, and then the hat-trick of Independent wins in 2024. Knockhill was a challenging weekend for us with reliability issues, but we came away knowing we had the pace to fight at the sharp end with a bit of luck on our side. Plenty of homework has been done back at base to put us back in the mix this weekend. These races are won & lost in the workshop, and I’m confident that once the car is in the window, we can challenge once again."


Gordon Shedden (#52) said: "It's good to be heading back to Donington, and to the venue of my first podium with Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport at the start of the year. The GP circuit offers something a bit different with the hairpin thrown in, and that opens up some interesting overtaking opportunities come race day. Knockhill was a highlight for us, with a strong Saturday and a solid race day, delivering another podium and an Independents win to the tally. We had good pace all weekend, so the focus now is on taking that performance, executing properly, and coming away with another big haul of points."

title.rendered: Dan Lloyd Returns to Restart Racing for Remainder of 2026 BTCC Season

excerpt.rendered: Restart Racing has confirmed that reigning BTCC Independent Drivers’ Champion...

content.rendered:
Restart Racing has confirmed that reigning BTCC Independent Drivers’ Champion Dan Lloyd will return to the team for the remainder of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season, replacing James Dorlin from this weekend’s event at Donington Park GP (22/23 August).

The change follows confirmation that Dorlin will step away from Restart Racing after six events with the team in 2026. He joined the squad at the beginning of the campaign alongside Chris Smiley and enjoyed Jack Sears Trophy success at Brands Hatch, before producing his strongest weekend of the season at Thruxton with three top-ten finishes, two Independents’ victories and another Jack Sears Trophy win.

Lloyd will now return to the wheel of a Hyundai i30 N Fastback, reuniting with Smiley and a team he knows extremely well after playing a central role in Restart Racing’s breakthrough 2025 season. He claimed the squad’s first outright BTCC victory with a memorable win at Silverstone before going on to secure the Independent Drivers’ Championship.

Together with Smiley, Lloyd also helped Restart Racing claim the Independent Teams’ Championship, completing a landmark campaign for the squad in only its second year of BTCC competition.

Although Lloyd stepped away from competing in the championship at the end of 2025, he has remained closely involved with Restart Racing throughout this season in an advisory role on race weekends.

Pete Jones, Team Principal of Restart Racing, said: “We’re absolutely delighted to have Dan back in the car. He knows the team, he knows the car and we know exactly what he is capable of. What we achieved together last year was incredibly special, so having the reigning Independent Champion back behind the wheel feels like a great fit for us.

“Dan has remained a big part of the team this year and has been with us at race weekends in an advisory role, so he has stayed very close to what we are doing and how the car has developed.

“He also has a brilliant relationship with everyone in the team and with Chris, which means he can come straight back in and get on with the job.

“We still have a lot we want to achieve this season and there are plenty of opportunities ahead of us. Bringing Dan back gives us a proven race winner who knows how to get the very best out of this car, and I think everyone in the team is excited to see what we can do together over the remaining rounds.”

Dan Lloyd said: “First of all, I want to say that I know this is a difficult situation for James. I’ve been in that position myself before in my career and I know how tough it can be. He’s a very talented driver and a great guy, and I genuinely wish him all the best for whatever comes next.

“From my side, I’m absolutely buzzing to be coming back. Restart Racing feels like home to me and what we achieved together last year was something I’ll never forget. To win the team’s first outright BTCC race and then finish the year as Independent Champion was incredibly special.

“I’ve stayed really close to the team this season, working with everyone at the race weekends, so I’ve never really felt like I’ve been away from it. That makes coming back into the car feel very natural.

“I know the Hyundai, I know the team, and I know how hard everyone works behind the scenes. I’m coming back hungry, I want to enjoy it and, most importantly, I want to help the team finish the season as strongly as we possibly can.

“I can’t wait to get back behind the wheel at Donington.”

Lloyd returns to BTCC action at Donington Park GP (22/23 August) as the championship enters its final four events of the 2026 campaign.

title.rendered: Donington Park GP sets the stage for crucial weekend in 2026 campaign

excerpt.rendered: Now or never for the chasing pack as Sutton looks...

content.rendered:
Now or never for the chasing pack as Sutton looks to tighten title grip

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship heads to Donington Park this weekend (22/23 August), returning to the scene of the action-packed season opener, but this time around it’s on the iconic GP layout.

It was Adam Morgan, Ash Sutton and Tom Chilton who shared the victories last time out, with the middle man extending his championship advantage over Tom Ingram and Dan Cammish.

Now, the full Donington Park Grand Prix circuit awaits as the season begins its run towards the finale.

Familiar Ground, Different Stakes

Donington Park provides a familiar setting this weekend, but the 2.49-mile Grand Prix configuration offers a very different test to the National circuit which opened the campaign back in April.

The longer configuration returned to the BTCC calendar in 2023 after more than two decades away, adding the Melbourne section and its heavy braking zones to the familiar rush through Redgate, the Craner Curves and the Old Hairpin. Three years on, the GP circuit once again arrives at a crucial stage of the season, with just four events remaining in the 2026 title fight.

Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK - Ford) heads back to a layout where he won the opening race on its championship return three years ago and still holds the quickest Qualifying lap there of 1m33.154s. This time, however, the four-time champion arrives with an 81-point advantage and the opportunity to take another significant step towards a record fifth Drivers’ crown.

Tom Ingram (Team VERTU - Hyundai) is the driver with the clearest task of stopping him. The reigning champion sits second on 246 points and won around the Grand Prix circuit last season, while his 1m33.621s effort from the same weekend is the current race lap record. With opportunities to close Sutton down beginning to run out, Donington offers an important chance to turn proven pace at the venue into a championship gain.

Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK - Ford) has his own recent Donington success to draw upon, having taken victory on the GP layout in 2024. Just 13 points now separate the #27 from Ingram, meaning another strong weekend could move the Yorkshireman into second while simultaneously strengthening NAPA Racing UK’s hand at the top of the Teams’ standings. The trio at the top of the standings have each taken two triumphs around the GP layout, the joint-most of any driver on the 2026 grid.

The battle immediately behind the leading trio is even tighter. Ricky Collard (Team VERTU – Hyundai) arrives fourth on 180 points, with Charles Rainford (WSR – BMW) on 169 and Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) on 167. Doble also returns to Donington having taken victory on the National circuit at the opening event of 2026, although the extended GP configuration presents a very different challenge this weekend.

That fight extends further down the order too, with just 30 points covering fourth to tenth in the Drivers’ Championship. Doble also arrives at Donington at the head of the Independent Drivers’ standings, while Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing – Audi) leads the way in the Jack Sears Trophy.

Saturday’s ‘Race to Pole’ means points are available before Sunday’s three contests even begin, adding another layer of importance to a weekend where recent Donington history, current form and an increasingly urgent title fight are set to collide.

TV, Timetables and Tickets

Complementing the tin top racing will be a sensational line-up of support series, as the Porsche Carrera Cup Great Britain, F4 British Championship certified by FIA MINI CHALLENGE Trophy and the Caterham Seven Championship UK complete the schedule of exciting races.

BTCC will be wowing the crowds both trackside and at home, with Saturday's 'Race to Pole' and the earlier qualifying session being streamed live via  ITV Sport's YouTube Channel from 1400, before ITV4's seven-and-a-half-hour race day broadcast gets underway at 1100 on Sunday.

Remember, continuing what started for the first time in the championship's history in 2025, the BTCC is being broadcast globally with every race being streamed live in 2026 via the BTCC YouTube Channel, whilst fans in North America can watch the action on the Racer Network. Look out for the races on Sunday starting at 1145, 1445 and 1730 (BST).

There's no place like being there, of course, and fans can purchase tickets in advance or on the gate throughout the weekend – visit here for more details.

title.rendered: Team VERTU takes victory from bruising Knockhill weekend

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU ended a challenging weekend on a high at...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU ended a challenging weekend on a high at Knockhill with a third victory of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season.

The EXCELR8-run team headed for the Scottish circuit chasing a big haul of points to close the gap at the top of the standings, with Tom Ingram sitting second in the Drivers’ Championship and Team VERTU holding the same position in the Teams’ Championship.

Ingram would be drawn in the first qualifying group, and ended up sixth quickest having lost his fastest time to track limits, with Ricky Collard ending up as the lead Team VERTU driver on the grid for the Qualifying Race when he went fourth quickest in group two.

That left Collard eighth on the grid with Ingram in eleventh, with Tom Chilton lining up in 14th and Nic Hamilton starting from 20th.

The Race to Pole itself would be a relatively subdued affair for the team, with Collard making up a spot at the start but ultimately ending the race where he started after being overhauled by Mikey Doble on the run to the line.

Ingram managed to gain two places as he climbed to ninth spot, with Chilton also gaining two positions to twelfth and Hamilton taking the flag in 20th.

Vastly different conditions greeted the team for the opening race of the weekend on Sunday with rain falling, as all four drivers were able to stay out of trouble when the lights went out at the start - despite Ingram being slightly slow away from the line.

Collard managed to climb as high as fourth in the early stages before being overhauled for position, and he then allowed Ingram through to take fifth before the finish with the defending champion having worked his way onto the rear of his teammate.

Chilton had hoped to join them in the top ten but was found in the gravel at the chicane and dropped to the back of the field, although a safety car period allowed him to close up the rear of the pack before battling his way through to 17th place at the finish.

An off-track moment for Hamilton left him to make an unscheduled trip to the pits before he finished a lap down in 22nd.

Conditions had improved by the time race two came around, but it would prove to be a short-lived affair for Ingram when he was caught out by cars ahead jumping on the brakes to get through the chicane on lap one, with the resultant contact being sufficient to damage the radiator on his car and put him into retirement.

That left Collard to lead the team’s challenge with a typically feisty performance that saw him battle his way to fourth spot before finally finding a way ahead of race one winner Adam Morgan to bag his sixth podium of the campaign.

Chilton gained five spots to race his way into the points in twelfth, with Hamilton having looked on course to finish just outside the points until his car ground to a halt exiting the chicane on the penultimate lap following a late safety car period.

The reverse grid draw saw Chilton put onto pole for the final race of the weekend, and he made the most of experience - alongside the softer compound tyre - pay dividends as he led the way from start-to-finish to score his first victory of the campaign.

From tenth on the grid, Collard battled his way to ninth place on the medium tyre, with Ingram - complete with a new engine - also on the slower tyre but able to charge his way through from the back of the grid to take tenth and grab a few points back from Sutton in the championship race.

Running on the soft tyre, Hamilton ended the weekend with his most competitive performance to fall just shy of a points finish, taking the flag second amongst the Jack Sears Trophy runners.

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “I’ve missed being on the top step of the podium so it’s nice to be taking a trophy home, particularly after it looked like it could be another of those weekends when I was facing the wrong way in the gravel in race one.

“When I got the reverse grid pole, I knew there was a real chance to go for the win, and I knew that I needed to make the most of the soft tyre in the early stages as I didn’t want to lose the opportunity. 

“I gave it everything and every lap was a qualifying lap to get the gap I needed, and even when the others closed in a bit later on, I’d been able to keep my TOCA Turbo Boost so I knew it was there if I needed it.

“Getting the win is great and is a good boost in confidence ahead of Donington Park GP, where I’ve gone well in recent years.”

Ricky Collard, #11 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “It’s been a good weekend for me across the board, and it helped that we had a stronger Saturday which meant I wasn’t trying to battle my way through the field as much on race day.

“To make it six podium finishes for the season and to move up to fourth in the championship standings is fantastic, and the team has done a great job this weekend to give me the tools that I needed.

“It’s great to see Tom Chilton get a win for the first time this season and it means everyone else in the team has been on the top step of the podium with Nic having his Jack Sears Trophy win. I’m the only one who hasn’t made it there yet, so I need to make sure I put that right!”

Nicolas Hamilton, #28 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “I turned up this weekend feeling really positive, but it’s been a difficult weekend with the changeable weather conditions. Free practice was a really positive start as I was half a second quicker than last season, and then I was quicker again in qualifying before the weather started to have an impact.

“When the rain arrived, I was on the back foot a bit because I don’t have the experience of the car in those conditions to really get the most from it. There are a lot of things that we need to think about with my car with the servo brake system and what bias we run, and in race one in particular when it was properly wet, I just didn’t feel comfortable.

“We were quicker in the second race and I felt more at home before the alternator failed right at the end, and the team did a great job to make some changes for race three where we tried something new that worked. I started from 19th and came through to 16th despite losing places at the start, which was a solid way to end things.

“Obviously it would have been nice to score a point, but it was still a good way to end a challenging weekend.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “As a team, it’s good to have come away from Knockhill with some trophies but it’s been a bruising weekend for me personally, and one where the only luck I had was bad luck. 

“Had it not been for track limits, we’d have been up on the third row of the grid for the qualifying race rather than stuck in the pack where it was hard to try and make progress with the amount of boost that we had.

“We had an issue with the car in race one that meant I didn’t get the best of starts but we still managed to climb to fifth, and then in race two going into the chicane, the guys in front concertinaed up and there was nowhere to go. It didn’t look like the biggest of hits but it did a lot of damage, and that was game over.

“Because of the issues in the first two races, we changed the engine for race three, and that is probably the high point of the weekend for me because the team did an outrageous job to get that sorted in 45 minutes - it was an unbelievable effort.

“To come from the back of the grid to finish in the top ten was good in terms of making up places, but obviously we’ve not scored the points we were hoping for this weekend which is disappointing. However, we’ll keep pushing hard and will come out fighting when we get to Donington Park in a few weeks time.”

title.rendered: Restart Racing battle through Knockhill race day

excerpt.rendered: Restart Racing battled through a thrilling day of mixed conditions...

content.rendered:
Restart Racing battled through a thrilling day of mixed conditions at Knockhill in the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, with Chris Smiley (#22) and James Dorlin (#132) scoring a double points finish.

The team entered Sunday encouraged by its strongest qualifying performance of the campaign. Smiley secured fourth in Saturday’s Race to Pole, while Dorlin would come 15th after contact whilst running in the top eight.

A heavy downpour shortly before the opening bout of race day left the circuit in treacherous conditions with limited visibility. The whole grid, including both Restart Racing Hyundai i30 N cars, started on wet tyres.

Smiley started from fourth but immediately dropped to fifth after Charles Rainford (WSR) passed him at Duffus Dip on the opening lap. Dorlin’s start differed, gaining two positions to move into 13th.

The difficult conditions soon began to affect the #22, who was struggling with a misted windscreen, causing visibility issues. After losing ground, Dorlin moved ahead of Smiley at Taylor’s Hairpin on lap seven, placing the duo 13th and 14th.

Smiley’s race became even more challenging when contact with Árón Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) saw him off the circuit at McIntyre’s. The Irishman recovered to 19th, while Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing) passed Dorlin as the pair continued to battle in the midfield.

The Yorkshireman initially crossed the line in 16th, directly ahead of Smiley in 17th. Both drivers were subsequently promoted one position following a penalty for NAPA Racing UK’s Dan Cammish, pushing the pair up one spot each.

With the circuit dry for the middle race of the day, both drivers switched to the soft tyre. Both drivers gained a position during a frenetic opening lap. The Safety Car was deployed to allow the stricken car of Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) to be recovered.

Racing resumed on lap five, with Smiley making strong progress through the order as he recovered from an early setback.

A string of overtakes lifted the Restart Racing driver into the top ten before he passed Cammish for ninth. His charge was brought to a premature end on lap 22, however, when damage sustained earlier in the race led to a front upright failure and sent him into the gravel at Duffus Dip.

The incident resulted in the team’s first retirement of the season and triggered a second Safety Car period. Dorlin also made ground following the restart, eventually taking the chequered flag in 14th.

Both cars ran the medium tyre for the final race, with Dorlin starting 14th and Smiley lining up 20th following his earlier retirement.

The #22 made immediate progress through the field, while Dorlin was shuffled back following contact with Daryl De Leon (WSR) in the opening laps.

The pair later found themselves in a close battle with championship leader Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK), with both Restart Racing cars briefly moving ahead during a lively scrap for the points-paying positions.

Smiley and Dorlin continued to run closely together through the closing stages but were unable to make further progress, eventually taking the chequered flag in 14th and 15th respectively to secure a double-points finish for the team.

Chris Smiley, #22 Restart Racing, said: “That’s Knockhill finished for another year. It promised to be one of our best weekends after the pace we showed in Qualifying and the Race to Pole.

“I started race one from fourth and unfortunately had an issue with my heated windscreen. I couldn’t see where I was going, so we fell back and eventually finished 16th.

“We made great progress in race two and climbed from 16th to ninth. I had a slight lock-up on some water on the inside at Taylor’s Hairpin and made unintentional contact with another car. That damaged the front upright, which then failed as I went into Duffus Dip and caused our first DNF of the season.

“We started race three from 20th on the medium tyre, and recovered to finish 14th. We’re going home feeling as though we’ve let a weekend get away from us because it could have delivered much more.”

James Dorlin, #132 Restart Racing, said: “Knockhill is done, and it had been a really, really tough weekend. We had the pace to be right at the front, but we weren’t in the right place at the right time and kept getting pushed around.

“In race three, we were moving forward during the opening laps and the car felt good. I was pushed wide on lap two; it compromised our race because, although we recovered several positions, we had lost too much ground through that initial contact.

“That’s touring car racing, unfortunately, especially around a circuit like Knockhill. It’s one to put behind us, and I’m really looking forward to Donington Park and seeing what we can achieve there.”

title.rendered: Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed - Knockhill

excerpt.rendered: The BTCC headed north to Knockhill for the sixth event...

content.rendered:
The BTCC headed north to Knockhill for the sixth event of the year, showcasing three spectacular races plus another thrilling Qualifying race in Scotland. The Fife rollercoaster delivered a frenetic, record-setting start to the second half of the season.

As the 2026 season continues to take full flight, take a listen to the sixth instalment of Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed, which was aired earlier this week (Tuesday, 11 August).

The podcast opened with none other than Adam Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing), as the Mercedes A35 Saloon driver took the new outfit's maiden BTCC triumph. The Lancastrian also headed the team's first one-two on Sunday after taking the fastest time in Qualifying and pole position after finishing first in the 'Race to Pole' a day prior.

Oly Collins (Team Manager, NAPA Racing UK) was the next guest on the show, speaking on the Alliance Racing-run squad not taking time off over the traditional summer break. Collins also spoke on Ash Sutton's impressive seven wins so far this campaign, commending the crew behind the four-time champ for their efforts to support the championship leader.

Alan Hyde also caught up with Tom Chilton (Team VERTU) after the Hyundai i30 N racer took his 19th career BTCC victory, with the most recent race going the way of the #3. Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing) was next on the show after a career-high weekend that saw the Scot's best single-race finish whilst also taking his highest-scoring weekend in the BTCC. Patterson's stablemate Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) also joined the show after a rollercoaster weekend left the Scot with a less-than-ideal result at his home venue.

Moffat and the rest of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship grid head to Donington Park (22/23 August) for the second visit to the circuit this year, this time around the GP layout for the seventh race weekend of the campaign.

title.rendered: WSR in top six on challenging Knockhill weekend

excerpt.rendered: WSR concluded a challenging mixed-weather Kwik Fit British Touring Car...

content.rendered:
WSR concluded a challenging mixed-weather Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship trip across the border to Knockhill, Scotland, with a trio of top-six finishes.

Drivers Charles Rainford and Daryl De Leon showed fighting spirit all the way aboard their BMW 330i M Sport cars in the final race of the weekend, securing more valuable points in the Independents Trophy with fifth and sixth places respectively.

Lewis Gilbert’s first BTCC outing on home soil was another learning curve for the 22-year-old, but the Ayrshire driver ended the weekend with an 18th-place finish after two retirements earlier in the day.

Rainford, sporting a special one-off livery for Knockhill, started the wet opener from sixth place but had to pit to remove a loose rear bumper after receiving a black flag with an orange disc at two-thirds distance, dropping him down the order.

A further spin after contact limited him to 21st at the flag, but a sensational charge through the field on the soft-compound tyre in race two brought the Horsham racer to sixth once again.

Another strong drive in the third race showcased the BMW's speed as Rainford secured a well-earned top-five result and his best of the day.

In race three, De Leon was also on the move after a frustrating second race, leaping 11 places to finish just behind Rainford in sixth.

The 20-year-old Anglo-Filipino, the reigning Jack Sears Trophy champion, had been in the mix for a solid top-six result in the opening bout before contact sent him through the gravel trap, relegating him to 11th.

Race two was a similar story as contact with Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK) saw De Leon off at Clark Corner, eventually resulting in a 17th-place result.

Competing with the support of the local crowd, Gilbert impressed in Saturday’s Qualifying Race, but did not finish Sunday’s opener after contact under braking for Clark.

Another incident in the second race of the day curtailed his chances of a points-scoring result. A learning weekend concluded with a deserved finish, after an early spin.

Charles Rainford: “We had amazing pace in Race One, but unfortunately, I had contact at the rear, which caused me to get a mechanical black flag, and then I had more contact after the Safety Car, which wasn’t ideal. I used that frustration in Race Two to get from 21st to sixth, and then I did the maximum I could in Race Three with a bit of damage. Overall, it had been a good day, with some nice points. We’ve been really good at Donington earlier in the year so hopefully we can repeat that pace next time out.”

Daryl De Leon: “It was a tough race day at Knockhill. We had some good pace in Race One, but with contact we lost three or four places. Then, in Race Two, I ended up in the barriers. Thankfully I managed to continue and finish 17th. In the final race, I was on the medium tyre and worked my way up to sixth from 17th with a lot of overtakes. Although the racing hadn’t gone our way this time, the atmosphere in Scotland has been amazing.”

Lewis Gilbert: “This weekend has been a good learning curve for me in the BTCC, especially in front of my home crowd - which was incredible. I was really happy with my pace in the final race, which was quite similar to the race winner on the same tyres. The first two races were a bit disappointing due to the issues, but we made a good step towards the end of the day, and I am already looking forward to getting back out there at Donington.”

Dick Bennetts, Team Principal: “It has been a good and bad day, but we can take the positives with all three cars reaching the finish in more or less one piece. Daryl had a strong final race, moving from 17th to sixth, and Charles was very impressive in the second race. For Lewis, it’s been another learning curve, and his pace was matching the leaders in Race Three, which is a big positive. The speed he has shown in the car with his limited experience has been incredible. Roll on Donington…”

title.rendered: Breakthrough weekend for Cataclean Plato Racing

excerpt.rendered: Rounds 16, 17 and 18 of the 2026 Kwik Fit...

content.rendered:
Rounds 16, 17 and 18 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship produced three different winners from three different teams, but it was Cataclean Plato Racing’s breakthrough weekend that stole the headlines at Knockhill.

Adam Morgan set the pace in qualifying, won Saturday afternoon’s ‘Race to Pole’ contest and then converted that form into victory in Sunday’s opening race.

The celebrations were further enhanced for the Mercedes squad as Dan Rowbottom completed a historic Cataclean Plato Racing one-two, with Team Principal and tin-top legend Jason Plato watching on.

The team’s strong form continued, while the remaining victories went to championship leader Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) and Tom Chilton (Team VERTU – Hyundai), as the BTCC title battle continued to take shape amid mixed conditions in Scotland.

Sutton is closing in on a potential record-breaking fifth overall drivers’ title and left the tight, twisty circuit with a firm grip on proceedings, while second-placed Tom Ingram lost ground to Dan Cammish.

Four-time champ Sutton holds an 81-point lead at the top of the order, whilst Cammish has closed to within 13 points of second placed Ingram.

Alliance Racing/Ford and its NAPA Racing UK outfit retain a commanding advantage at the top of both the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ standings, while Mikey Doble and LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing remain in control of the Independents’ honours.

Dexter Patterson also enjoyed a standout weekend, pulling clear of James Dorlin in the race for the Jack Sears Trophy.

The BTCC returns to action in two weeks’ time, on 22/23 August, at Donington Park.

Morgan survives the showers for first Cataclean Plato Racing victory

Lancastrian Morgan claimed victory in the Knockhill opener, securing Cataclean Plato Racing’s first win while leading home a one-two finish ahead of teammate Rowbottom.

The success is testament to the hard work put in by the rookie squad, and particularly the progress made with the Mercedes A35 Saloons since the mid-summer break.

Morgan had to contend with wet conditions and a late race safety car intervention, but the multiple race winner was always in control of the contest, as Rowbottom played rear gunner in the closing laps.

Rowbottom had earlier relinquished Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport's Gordon Shedden of second with an impressive move, whilst the Scotsman then had to turn his attentions to his rear mirrors.

Incredibly, there were nine Drivers' titles between the racers battling for third at the finish, as Toyota man Shedden saw off the challenges from the title chasing duo of Sutton (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) and Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai).

Sutton had got the better of Ingram in the earlier running with the former charging up through the order from 11th on the grid.

A series of stellar moves in extreme conditions looked set to secure another rostrum finish for the #116 Ford Focus Titanium, but as Ingram’s #80 Hyundai i30N gradually closed in, Sutton’s focus shifted to keeping his old adversary behind.

Seventh heaven for Sutton

NAPA Racing UK's Sutton surged to victory in Round 17, to take his seventh race win of the campaign and extend his advantage at the top of the standings.

Starting from fourth on the grid, Sutton’s Ford made light work of Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport – Toyota) and Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing – Mercedes) ahead of him before he set about attacking Rowbottom (Cataclean Plato Racing – Mercedes) for the lead.

There was disappointment behind for Sutton’s main title rival, Team VERTU’s Ingram, who was already nursing a power issue off the line before being forced into retirement after contact. As the field concertinaed ahead, the #80 Hyundai ran into the rear of Shedden’s Toyota on the first run to the chicane and was immediately forced to pit with radiator damage.

Rowbottom performed extremely well in the #32 Mercedes A35 Saloon out front, particularly considering the lack of boost available while also running the harder Goodyear tyre compound.

There was little Rowbottom could do to stop his former teammate however, as Sutton's #116 Ford Focus Titanium sliced down the inside at the final hairpin.

Two safety car periods interrupted proceedings with the second delay only allowing for a final one-lap shootout at the finish.

Sutton cruised home while Rowbottom fended off the Hyundai of Team VERTU's Ricky Collard, who again continued his impressive BTCC season in style.

Chilton charges to first victory of 2026

Team VERTU's Chilton took his 19th career BTCC triumph and the third of his career at Knockhill.

The experienced tin top star has endured a mixed 2026 campaign so far with a solitary podium at Snetterton being a high point, but those misfortunes are now a thing of the past as the #3 Hyundai driver dominated the finale in Scotland.

If Chilton was pleased with his pillar-to-post triumph then Morgan was overjoyed with his weekend's work as he ended the day with a second place, following on from his 'Race to Pole' win, race one victory and another top five finish – comfortably the Cataclean Plato Racing driver's best weekend of the season so far.

The podium was completed by NAPA Racing UK’s Dan Cammish as the Ford driver closed in on Ingram in the overall standings.

Patterson was another to round off a fantastic weekend at his home circuit as the Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing Audi driver claimed fourth and with it the Jack Sears Trophy honours, following two top eight results earlier in the day.

The WSR duo of Charles Rainford and Daryl De Leon finished proceedings north of the border in solid form with fifth and sixth respectively, whilst Rowbottom completed a great weekend for Cataclean Plato Racing with seventh.

Adam Morgan, Cataclean Plato Racing, said: “I am completely blown away. A pole position, a race win, a second and a fifth. That has got to be up there with the biggest points haul I’ve ever had. I’ve been doing this for a long time so just to get a pole position was amazing but to top it off with a win and a second is just mind-blowing. It’s a huge credit to the team, the sponsors and everybody involved – a huge thank you.”

title.rendered: Moffat leads Scottish one-two at Knockhill

excerpt.rendered: There was double joy for both Scotland and Power Maxed...

content.rendered:
There was double joy for both Scotland and Power Maxed Racing in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship Practice Session at Knockhill as Aiden Moffat led home Audi stablemate Dexter Patterson at the top of the timesheets.

The fast and frenetic 50-minute session saw all 23 cars take to the track with hundreds of miles completed around the undulating Fife circuit.

Times improved rapidly as the session wore on with the EXCELR8 Motorsport duo of Tom Ingram and Ricky Collard both enjoying brief spells at the top, whilst the Cataclean Plato Racing duo of Dan Rowbottom and Adam Morgan held a one-two of their own in the closing 15 minutes, as the Mercedes-run squad continue to show improved performance.

It was the Audi PMR outfit that kept its powder dry until the final ten minutes as Moffat, Patterson and Doble all fired in fantastic times.

LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing’s Moffat earned the final bragging rights as his 50.840s lap time dipped under Ash Sutton’s race lap record from 2020, whilst Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing’s Patterson ended up just 0.080s off the benchmark.

Rowbottom secured third ahead of Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing), whilst Morgan completed an-all Audi-Mercedes top five.

Impressively, Chris Smiley was the best of the rest in the Restart Racing Hyundai, ahead of reigning champion Ingram in the same i30N machine.

Daryl De Leon (WSR), Aron Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) and Collard (EXCELR8 Motorsport) completed the top ten positions.

As a reminder, the finishing order of Free Practice is now split into two groups, odd-finishing-numbers (Group 1) and even-finishing-numbers (Group 2), for a 15-minute qualifying session to set their fastest times.

The group with the fastest qualifying time will occupy the odd-numbered grid positions for the Qualifying Race, ordered by their respective qualifying times. The other group will occupy the even-numbered grid positions, also ordered by qualifying times.

15 minutes after the qualifying session for Group 2 has concluded, the standard grid procedure for a race start begins, and the pit lane opens. The finishing order of the shorter 17 lap ‘Race to Pole’ will determine the grid for the first of Sunday’s traditional trio of races.

Half-points are awarded for the Qualifying Race. There are no bonus points for leading a lap, the fastest lap, or for pole position for the Qualifying Race, whereas the bonus points for leading a lap and the fastest lap are still available on Sunday.

Qualifying and the Qualifying Race can be found LIVE on the ITV Sport YouTube Channel worldwide from 13:50 later today.

Mercedes man Morgan showed the upturn in pace for the rookie outfit with his second overall career pole in Britain's elite motorsport championship, whilst teammate Dan Rowbottom confirmed the squad's speed with third at the finish.

There was local joy too as Gordon Shedden's Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport Toyota was sandwiched between the two 'Silver Arrows' at the conclusion of the 20-lap race.

It was almost a one-two for Cataclean Plato Racing with Rowbottom running side-by-side with Shedden across the start/finish line for the penultimate time, but the three time champion used his quality and experience to hold off his rival.

There was drama on the opening tour when Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) and Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing) were both fired off track in separate incidents, the latter involving a heavy hit into the barrier for his Toyota at the chicane.

The top three positions remained settled following the restart but there was a quick change behind as Chris Smiley (Restart Racing) scythed by Charles Rainford's WSR BMW for fourth at the final hairpin.

The WSR pairing of Rainford and Daryl De Leon eventually had to settle for fifth and sixth, as the 330i M Sports showed good consistency rather than race-winning pace, whilst the fight for seventh kicked off behind.

It was Mikey Doble that won that particular battle as he got the draft out of the final hairpin on the last lap. The #88 Audi A3 Saloon ran side-by-side with Ricky Collard's Team VERTU Hyundai across the line and incredibly took the place by just 0.006s, whilst reigning champion Tom Ingram (Team VERTU) looked on from behind.

Dan Cammish resisted the pressure from NAPA Racing UK teammate Ash Sutton to take a top ten finish, with the Ford Focus Titanium duo separated by less than half a second.

Full credit, however, went to Morgan as he not only claimed his first qualifying success for eight years, but he also secured the second 'Race to Pole' triumph for Cataclean Plato Racing. The Cheshire driver had finished either sixth or seventh in the previous Qualifying Races so far this season so today's performance represented a huge turnaround for the multiple race winner.

Rounds 16, 17 and 18 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship take place at Knockhill tomorrow with the action getting underway in the UK on ITV4 from 11:15. The races will also be beamed around the world on Racer TV (North America) and the BTCC YouTube Channel (Rest of the World).

Adam Morgan, Cataclean Plato Racing, said: "It's mega. The car is in a lovely spot here. It's allowing you to use the kerbs, it's got really good traction and I've just been able to really get on top of it. My first pole position was back at Rockingham in 2018, so we've had to wait a while, but we've finally done it. It's a great start to the weekend for Dan (Rowbottom) and I and we can hopefully keep moving forward. I think we're in a good place. We're back!"

Knockhill - Qualifying Race - Classification:

Penalties:

Qualifying Race

Josh Cook and Speedworks Corolla Racing were investigated in the Qualifying Race at Knockhill, for adjusting the car while under Parc Fermé conditions. The Clerk determined that there had been a contravention of the regulations, but no further action was taken, due only to the fact that the normal penalty would have no actual effect - Click here for the penalty report.

Thruxton

Adam Morgan, Josh Cook, Árón Taylor-Smith and Mikey Doble were investigated for an incident in Round 15 of the championship; the Clerk deemed that no one driver was predominantly responsible for the collision. The Clerk determined it to be a racing incident - Click here for the penalty report.

Ryan Bensley and Speedworks Corolla Racing were investigated in Round 15 of the championship for releasing the car in an unsafe condition. The Team Principal fully accepted the team’s failure and the Clerk accepted the Team Principal’s apology and explanation - Click here for the penalty report.

title.rendered: Team VERTU Targets Top Step in Scotland

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU will look to add to an impressive record...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU will look to add to an impressive record of success at Knockhill when the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship makes the annual visit to Scotland this weekend for the sixth event of the season.

The EXCELR8-run team crosses the border seeking to strengthen its title challenge, with defending champion Tom Ingram currently sitting second in the Drivers’ standings and Team VERTU having moved into the same position in the Teams’ Championship following the previous meeting at Thruxton.

Ingram fought his way to a second victory of the year last time out in Hampshire but finds himself playing catch-up to long-time rival Ash Sutton in the standings at the halfway stage of the season.

The two-time champion’s record at Knockhill includes an impressive victory last season, the largest winning margin seen that year, whilst he has picked up a total of seven podium finishes at the Fife venue.

Ricky Collard remains the second-highest Team VERTU driver in the standings having moved up to fifth spot at Thruxton, where he battled back from a retirement in the Qualifying Race to bag a best finish of fourth.

The former British GT Champion is seeking to add to an impressive record of five podium finishes already this year – more than doubling his career tally through the first half of the season.

Like Ingram, Tom Chilton is a multiple winner at Knockhill through the years, having made his first outing at the circuit back in 2002.

Chilton rebounded well to pick up three points finishes in Hampshire after a troublesome Qualifying Race of his own, but has so far managed just a single podium finish this year to sit 13th in the standings.

Nicolas Hamilton enjoyed another productive weekend at Thruxton as he secured points for the fourth successive event, meaning he has already surpassed his previous best for points scored in a season.

Hamilton also moved up into third place in the Jack Sears Trophy and makes the trip to Scotland with confidence on a high at a circuit he admits is one of his favourites on the calendar.

Three solid finishes remain his first target for the weekend to maintain the impressive progress he has made since joining the team at the start of the season, with the ultimate goal being to extend his points-scoring run.

Saturday’s qualifying session and qualifying race are scheduled to take place from 14:00 and will air live on YouTube, with the three races on Sunday being aired live on ITV4 at 11:15, 14:15 and 17:20.

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “The issues we had in the qualifying race at Thruxton really hampered our chances on race day but we battled back well to get up into the top ten – although that’s not where I was hoping to be.

“Heading to Knockhill, I’m hoping for a more trouble-free weekend which will allow us to really make the most of the pace we have in the car. Last season we managed to come from the back of the grid to take a pair of top eight finishes so if we can qualify well, there is no reason why we can’t expect to be near the front.

“Knockhill is a circuit that I have always enjoyed and where I’ve scored silverware in the past. The target is to try and add to that this weekend.”

Ricky Collard, #11 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “On my last visit to Knockhill in 2023, I picked up a podium finish and had my best weekend of the season, and I also won there whilst competing in British F4, so there are plenty of fond memories from earlier in my career.

“Heading back to Scotland this time around, I’m feeling confident about my chances of another strong performance to build on what has been a really positive season so far.

“The Hyundai is a proven race winner at Knockhill and having missed out on a podium at Thruxton, my target is to get back into the top three and battle for some trophies.”

Nicolas Hamilton, #28 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Thruxton was one of the events I was least looking forward to and I managed to come away with some points, which leaves me confident going to Knockhill – which is a circuit I love.

“The Scottish crowd is great and the track is amazing; it’s like being on a giant rollercoaster where you’re constantly on two wheels and there is always something going on.

“Obviously I’ve not driven the Hyundai there before as has been the case with most of the circuits that we’ve visited, but I’m confident that we are going to have a strong package and I’m really excited to see what we can achieve in terms of results.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Thruxton was a stronger weekend for us than the results on paper suggest, even with the victory in the final race, and we now head for Knockhill hoping to build on the positive results we have gained there in the past.

“Going into the second half of the season, we know there is a huge challenge ahead of us as we look to close the gap at the top of the standings but the whole team is focused on going the best job we can do over the remaining five rounds.

“Track position is key at Knockhill so it’s going to be important to try and maximise our performance during Saturday to ensure that we are towards the sharp end of the grid when it comes to Sunday’s three races.

“I’ve been around the BTCC long enough to know how quickly things can change and one difficult weekend can have a big impact – as I’ve seen personally this year already. With that in mind, we’ve got to push hard to ensure that we pick up as many points as possible this weekend to strengthen our position.”

title.rendered: WSR raring to go as Gilbert faces home-soil debut

excerpt.rendered: WSR anticipate raucous local support this weekend for local driver...

content.rendered:
WSR anticipate raucous local support this weekend for local driver Lewis Gilbert as the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship ventures north of the border for its annual Scottish event at Knockhill.

The triple-header race weekend at the Fife circuit marks the beginning of the second half of the season for the UK’s most popular racing series and gives the 18-time champions a great opportunity to add to their two wins so far in 2026.

Scottish rookie Gilbert, who is joined by team-mates Charles Rainford and Dary De Leon, is excited for what is only his second BTCC event; the Dalry, North Ayrshire, driver having switched to touring cars from single-seaters less than a month ago.

The 22-year-old came close to scoring points on his BTCC debut last time out at Thruxton and is eager to make good on his promise in front of his home crowd aboard his BMW 330i M Sport.

Team-mates Rainford and De Leon are both eager to return to the podium after enduring frustrating weekends at Thruxton last time out.

The former has won twice in 2026 aboard his BMW 330i M Sport – those victories coming at Snetterton and Oulton Park ahead of the summer break – and the Horsham racer is determined to achieve more success in Scotland.

Rainford headed an all-WSR top three to score his first career BTCC pole position at the 1.3-mile circuit last year, adding a second-place finish and setting the fastest race lap of the event.

De Leon, meanwhile, started second – his maiden front-row qualifying result – and scored valuable Jack Sears Trophy points during a campaign in which he would eventually become class champion.

The Anglo-Filipino, who turned 21 this week, was a double podium-finisher at Snetterton and is currently second in the Independent Drivers’ points

WSR have the best record of any current BTCC team at Knockhill with 19 race wins, including double victories in each of the past three seasons, and pole positions in four of the past five visits to the track.

Lewis Gilbert (#29): “It’s pretty cool that in only my second event in the BTCC, I have the chance to race at my home track. Knockhill’s about an hour away from where I live so it’s as local as it gets for me. Although I’ve never raced there, I’ve done a rally and I’ve driven the circuit on track days so I’m familiar with the layout and it’s a pretty testing one for just over a mile. I’ve watched BTCC at Knockhill before there and always noticed how great the support is for Scottish drivers, so hopefully we can get some good results to really get the crowd cheering.”

Charles Rainford (#99): “I can’t wait to get to Knockhill and to the scene of my first BTCC pole position last year. After the challenging time we had at Thruxton, I’ll be very glad to be back a tight and twisty track that should suit our BMWs down to the ground. Last year it was podiums and fastest laps for me in Scotland, but this time I’m determined to get that big ‘Number One’ board and come away with a win.”

Daryl De Leon (#2): “Going from Thruxton to Knockhill is pretty much the biggest change you can get in the BTCC – the two tracks are the total opposite. I don’t mind that, though, as Knockhill should be really good for our BMWs. The rear-wheel-drive layout means we can put the power down really well out of the hairpin and get a good slingshot up the straight. After qualifying on the front row last year, I’m setting my targets nice and high.”

title.rendered: Driven by Sport welcomes families to Thruxton

excerpt.rendered: The new-for-2026 community initiative, Driven by Sport presented by Kwik...

content.rendered:
The new-for-2026 community initiative, Driven by Sport presented by Kwik Fit, continued its successful inaugural year with an engaging and inspiring event at Thruxton Circuit last month.

Held in the school holidays for the first time, the event offered a fresh BTCC-inspired experience, with local children attending alongside their parents and a number of competition winners securing places through the BTCC website and social media channels.

Guests once again enjoyed a broad range of STEM-led and interactive activities, each offering an engaging insight into the many roles and career opportunities available across motorsport.

These included engineering, first aid, car design, tyre technology, television presenting and, of course, the ever-popular sim racing experience. Furthermore, it wasn’t just the kids joining in with the fun this time around as the parents took on the challenges too, making for an unforgettable family experience for those in attendance.

Attendees also had the opportunity to meet BTCC driver Dan Rowbottom, get close to the championship’s racing cars and enjoy a behind-the-scenes look at life inside the BTCC paddock. In particular, guests got to speak to Power Maxed Racing driver Mikey Doble and his team in their garage, with the opportunity to apply ‘Driven by Sport’ stickers to one of the cars seen across the world all weekend.

The hands-on career discovery programme for school-age students combines education and entertainment through immersive, motorsport-themed experiences delivered by industry professionals, showcasing the many pathways into the sport.

The Thruxton event formed part of a growing programme of community-focused activities organised by the BTCC, including school and hospital visits, charitable events and further Driven by Sport experiences.

By welcoming parents and the wider BTCC community on this occasion, the programme – presented by BTCC Title Partner Kwik Fit – was able to introduce an even broader audience to the diverse skills and careers that contribute to the success of the championship.

title.rendered: Where to Watch: Knockhill

excerpt.rendered: The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship shoots north...

content.rendered:
The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship shoots north of the border to Knockhill this weekend (8/9 August) for the sixth event of the year, kickstarting the second half of the campaign.

After three different victors at Thruxton, the BTCC heads to the Fife rollercoaster as Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK) leads the way for a rampant weekend of action around the 1.27-mile circuit.

The weekend gets underway with Free Practice, then we go straight into qualifying. Two groups of 15-minute sessions, split according to the finishing order from Free Practice between odd and even finishing positions. The group with the fastest time will take the odd-numbered grid spots for the Qualifying Race. 15 minutes after qualifying, the pit lane opens ahead of the ‘Race for Pole’. A 17-lap race will then take place with half points awarded, as the result forms the grid for the first of the traditional trio of races on Sunday.

Last time out, the 2026 grid headed to Hampshire for the fifth race weekend of the championship. After another sensational Saturday, culminating in the all-new ‘Race to Pole’, Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing) would take his maiden Qualifying Race victory, setting Sunday up for the perfect start as the Toyota Corolla GR Sport driver then took his first victory of the season. Championship leader Sutton would stand triumphant in Race 2, with a performance that saw the four-time champ yet again extend his lead in the standings. The final race of the weekend saw Tom Ingram (Team VERTU) take his second victory of the campaign, to slow the bleed of championship points his title rival had gained.

This weekend’s race day action will feature on the home of the BTCC, ITV4, from 1030 on Sunday (9 August), while the ITV YouTube page will host the Qualifying Race and Qualifying on Saturday (8 August) from 1400.

As in 2025, each race day of the season – including all support series’ races – will be streamed LIVE around the globe on the BTCC YouTube channel, with the exception of the UK and North America, which have existing broadcast arrangements.

The BTCC will be aired LIVE in North America (US and Canada), continuing the multi-year agreement with the RACER Network, streaming live and on demand as part of a long-term agreement with the championship.

All 30 races are scheduled to air on the main RACER channel, whilst support series’ and extended BTCC highlights will be available to watch via the RACER+ App, the network’s premium motorsports streaming platform. Race 1 will begin at 06:15 Eastern Time (ET) with Race 2 following at 09:15 ET and Race 3 closing out the day’s racing at 12:20 ET.

Click here for the full TV guide for Knockhill

title.rendered: Action-Packed Knockhill Awaits for Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport

excerpt.rendered: Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport heads north of the...

content.rendered:
Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport heads north of the border this week as the team prepares to contest event six of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Knockhill (8/9 August).

The annual trip to the fan-favourite Scottish venue sees the team return to the 1.27-mile circuit in Fife, just north of Edinburgh. One of the shortest tracks on the BTCC calendar, Knockhill is also among the most demanding, with its narrow, undulating layout and unique character making it a favourite for both drivers and fans alike.

Following a hard-fought weekend at Thruxton, both Gordon Shedden and Árón Taylor-Smith will be aiming to bounce back and return to the sharp end of the grid after showing encouraging pace at the high-speed Hampshire circuit.

Home favourite and three-time BTCC champion Shedden boasts an impressive record at Knockhill, having claimed four race victories and 11 podium finishes at his home circuit during his illustrious career so far. The Scotsman will be hoping to add to that tally in front of his home crowd this weekend.

Alongside 'Flash', Irishman Taylor-Smith also has fond memories of the Fife venue. An Independents class winner at the venue in 2023, he has consistently scored strong points and will be looking to build on that record this weekend.

Heading into event six, Shedden sits ninth in the Drivers' Championship, with Taylor-Smith occupying 12th. Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport remains fifth in the Teams' Championship and third in the Independent Teams' Championship, with the team focused on closing the gap in both standings as the season enters its second half.

Following Saturday morning's opening 50-minute Free Practice session (10:30), the all-important Qualifying Groups (14:05) and 17-lap Qualifying Race (15:05) will determine the grid for Sunday's three races.


Sunday's races are scheduled for 11:15, 14:15 and 17:20, with all three contests broadcast live on ITV4 and ITVX in the UK, Racer Network in North America and the BTCC YouTube channel anywhere else in the world.

Árón Taylor-Smith (#50) said:

“Knockhill is a unique circuit that always throws up plenty of challenges, but it’s one I really enjoy. I can’t wait to get back out there and see what we are capable of this weekend.

“We’ve shown throughout the season that we have strong race pace, and if we can back that up with a solid qualifying performance on Saturday, we’ll give ourselves every chance of fighting at the front.


“I’ve had some good results here in the past, so the aim is to keep building our momentum, come away with some strong points, and continue moving in the right direction.”

Gordon Shedden (#52) said:


“I can’t wait to get out on track this weekend in front of the home crowd. Knockhill is always one of the highlights of the season for me. I’ve had plenty of success there over the years, and there’s nothing quite like bringing the BTCC to Scotland.

“Our race pace has been strong this season, with a win, Independent victories and podium finishes proving what we’re capable of. The key now is qualifying further up the grid because we know we have the pace to fight at the front.

“If we execute the weekend well and maximise every opportunity, I’m confident we can be in the mix for podiums and give the Scottish fans something to cheer about.”

title.rendered: BTCC Heads North for Knockhill Thriller

excerpt.rendered: Knockhill’s rollercoaster layout sets the stage for the next chapter...

content.rendered:
Knockhill’s rollercoaster layout sets the stage for the next chapter of the 2026 title fight


The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship now heads to Knockhill this weekend (8/9 August), after three pulsating races at Thruxton launched the second half of the season in spectacular style.

Hampshire’s speedbowl saw Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing - Toyota), Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK - Ford) and Tom Ingram (Team VERTU - Hyundai) each claim victory.

It was Cook, the ‘King of Thruxton’, who immediately took to the fore last time out, setting a time in Qualifying only 0.018 seconds shy of the all-time record to start the ‘Race to Pole’ from the front. The Toyota Corolla GR Sport driver stayed true to his nickname in the Qualifying Race, leading from lights to flag to start race day with a clear view.

Sunday started in similar fashion, as Cook once again led from start to finish to extend his record number of triumphs at the circuit to 11, whilst becoming the eighth winner of 2026 in just 13 races. Sutton stalked the #66 throughout the race to come home second as Daniel Rowbottom (Cataclean Plato Racing - Mercedes) took the team’s maiden podium in the BTCC.


After coming close in the opening bout, the championship leader would make his presence felt in the second race of the day, immediately taking the lead from Cook on the first run up to the Club chicane. Eventually, Sutton would cross the line with a 9.305-second lead as Ingram was handed a ten-second time penalty for track-limits infringements, dropping him from second to fifth.

The final race of the UK’s premier motorsport championship’s return to action favoured Ingram differently than the two previous contests. Starting second in the reverse-grid race, the Team VERTU star would take the lead from polesitter James Dorlin (Restart Racing - Hyundai) before reaching the first braking point at Campbell. The reigning champion would go on to take victory as the field behind fought robustly, leaving Ingram out in front to score vital points in his championship challenge.

Across the grid, NAPA Racing UK continues to lead the Teams’ Championship, while Alliance Racing/Ford remains at the head of the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ standings. LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing also retains its advantage in the Independent Teams’ order.

Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing - Audi) continues to lead the Independent Drivers’ Championship, while James Dorlin now tops the Jack Sears Trophy standings by two points.

With the high-speed challenge of Thruxton now complete, the BTCC heads north to Knockhill. The undulating Scottish circuit promises another action-packed weekend as the second half of the 2026 campaign continues.

Conquering the Crests

One man knows Knockhill’s bumps, brows and blind crests better than any other driver on the grid, three-time champion Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport - Toyota).

The Scottish favourite has four victories at his home venue, with his most recent coming back in 2015. Now in his second season in Toyota machinery, the #52 will be one to watch in Fife.

Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing - Audi) is another fan favourite heading home after a difficult weekend in Hampshire. The man who holds the record as the championship’s youngest race starter will be looking for a repeat of his early season form that saw him lift silverware.

Another Scot heading homebound is Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing - Audi), who, up until the opening weekend of this season in new machinery, had his best result in the BTCC at Knockhill. Now two points adrift from the top of the Jack Sears Trophy lead, the #17 will be eager for another career-best in front of his home crowd.

The fourth and by no means least of the Scottish drivers is BTCC newcomer Lewis Gilbert (WSR - BMW). The three-time race starter heads to his second event in the championship after narrowly missing out on points on his debut weekend at Thruxton.

TV, Timetables and Tickets

Complementing the tin top racing will be a sensational line-up of support series, as the Porsche Sprint Challenge Great Britain, MINI CHALLENGE, Caterham 7 Championship UK and Scottish Legends Championship complete the schedule of exciting races.

BTCC will be wowing the crowds both trackside and at home, with Saturday's 'Race to Pole' and the earlier qualifying session being streamed live via ITV Sport's YouTube Channel from 1400, before ITV4's seven-and-a-half-hour race day broadcast gets underway at 1030 on Sunday.

Remember, continuing what started for the first time in the championship's history in 2025, the BTCC is being broadcast globally with every race being streamed live in 2026 via the BTCC YouTube Channel, whilst fans in North America can watch the action on the Racer Network. Look out for the races on Sunday starting at 1115, 1415 and 1720 (BST).

There's no place like being there of course, and fans can purchase tickets in advance or on the gate throughout the weekend – visit here for more details.

title.rendered: Pole, Victory and Podium for Speedworks Corolla Racing at Thruxton

excerpt.rendered: Speedworks Corolla Racing enjoyed one of its strongest weekends of...

content.rendered:
Speedworks Corolla Racing enjoyed one of its strongest weekends of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season at Thruxton, with Josh Cook delivering a dominant display that included pole position, a race win and a podium finish, while Ryan Bensley made an encouraging BTCC debut with the Cheshire-based squad.

The UK's fastest circuit provided the perfect stage for the Toyota Corolla GR Sport to showcase its pace, with the team immediately establishing itself as the benchmark during Saturday's qualifying session.

Cook produced a sensational lap to secure pole position from title rival Tom Ingram (Team VERTU), underlining both his confidence around Thruxton and the outright performance of the Speedworks-run package.

Alongside him, Bensley enjoyed an encouraging first qualifying session for the team, securing 17th on the grid, making his competitive debut in the #7 and continuing to build experience in touring cars.

Cook converted the prime starting position into pole position during Saturday's Race to Pole encounter, successfully absorbing relentless pressure from both Ingram and Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK) throughout the contest. Rarely afforded a moment to relax, Cook produced a flawless drive to secure maximum points ahead of Sunday's opening race.

Unfortunately, Bensley's Race to Pole ended prematurely following contact, forcing an early retirement despite another encouraging display.

Sunday began in equally impressive fashion as the #66 once again demonstrated his race craft and composure to convert pole position into victory in race one.

Although Sutton remained firmly within striking distance throughout the race, Cook never faltered, controlling the pace superbly to secure the first victory of the weekend.

Bensley continued his learning process by bringing the Corolla home in 19th position after another competitive midfield performance.

Race two presented a fresh challenge, with significantly reduced boost available to Cook following his earlier success. The Bath-born driver would end the bout in third after being penalised for an incident involving Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK), dropping from second to the third step of the podium.

Bensley was once again involved in close midfield battles throughout the race, overcoming contact and continuing to gain valuable experience before finishing 19th, narrowly missing out on his maiden BTCC championship points.

The reverse-grid finale promised another opportunity for silverware. Cook made an excellent start and quickly established himself inside the leading group, looking well placed to challenge for another podium before contact at the final chicane ended his weekend early.

Bensley's weekend also ended prematurely after contact with Lewis Selby (NAPA Racing UK) caused his retirement just three laps into the final bout of the weekend.

Despite the disappointment of the closing encounter, Speedworks Corolla Racing leaves Hampshire with considerable encouragement. Pole position, triumphs in both the Race to Pole and race one, together with a further podium finish, represent the team's strongest points hauls of the season, while Bensley's pace and professionalism on his debut provide plenty of optimism heading into the remainder of the championship.

Christian Dick, Team Principal, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "Thruxton was a weekend that really demonstrated what this team is capable of. Josh was exceptional from the moment the weekend began. Fastest in Qualifying by that margin around a circuit like Thruxton is something very special, and to follow that with victories in both the Race to Pole and Race One was a fantastic reward for everyone's hard work."

"Naturally we're disappointed with how the final race unfolded because another podium - and potentially even more - looked within reach before the contact. Even so, the pace we showed throughout the weekend gives us enormous confidence heading into the next rounds."

"Ryan also deserves a huge amount of credit. Stepping into the BTCC midway through the season is never easy, but he integrated into the team brilliantly, showed genuine speed and approached the weekend with real maturity. The results don't quite tell the full story, and we're all excited to see how quickly he continues to develop."

Josh Cook, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "Overall, it's been a really satisfying weekend. To take pole position, win the Race to Pole and then convert that into another victory on Sunday is exactly what we set out to achieve."

"The team gave me a fantastic car all weekend and it was capable of fighting at the front in every session. It's obviously frustrating to lose second place in Race Two through the penalty and then have Race Three end the way it did because we were right back in the fight again."

"Even so, there are plenty of positives to take away. The pace of the Corolla was excellent, and we'll head to Knockhill feeling confident."

Ryan Bensley, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "It's been a huge learning weekend, but one I've really enjoyed. Joining a team midway through the season is never straightforward, but everyone at Speedworks made me feel welcome from the outset."

"Qualifying gave me confidence that the pace is there, and although the races didn't quite fall our way with the incidents we experienced, I learned something every time I went out on track."

"The Toyota felt stronger every session, and I'm already looking forward to Knockhill. I know there's much more to come once I build more experience with both the car and the championship."

title.rendered: Listen Again: Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed - Thruxton

excerpt.rendered: The BTCC returned from its traditional summer break for the...

content.rendered:
The BTCC returned from its traditional summer break for the fifth event of the year, showcasing three spectacular races plus another thrilling Qualifying race at Thruxton. The UK's fastest circuit delivered a fantastic, fast and furious bookend to the first half of the season.

As the 2026 season continues to take full flight, take a listen to the fifth instalment of Tin Top Tuesday powered by Power Maxed, which was aired earlier this week (Tuesday, 28 July).

The podcast opened with none other than Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing) as the Toyota Corolla GR Sport racer further solidified his status as the 'King of Thruxton', taking the fastest time in Qualifying, pole position after finishing first in the 'Race to Pole', and taking victory in the first race of the weekend. Cook now has 11 victories at the Hampshire venue, extending his ever-impressive record.

Nick Halstead (Steal Seel with Power Maxed Racing) was the next guest on the show, speaking ahead of his return to the championship after 307 days away from competing in the UK's premier motorsport series. After Halstead's time away, his entry into the 2026 campaign sees Power Maxed Racing become a four-car outfit for the first time in its history.

Alan Hyde also caught up with Matt James (Editor, Motorsport News), reviewing the season at the halfway stage. Lewis Gilbert (WSR) also joined the show as the BMW driver spoke on his debut BTCC weekend, whilst immediately pre-empting travelling straight to his home event at Knockhill in a week's time. Gilbert and the rest of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship grid head to the Scottish venue of Knockhill (8/9 August) for the sixth race weekend of the campaign.

title.rendered: Doble speeds to fourth Independent triumph of 2026

excerpt.rendered: Mikey Doble remains the driver to beat in the Independents...

content.rendered:
Mikey Doble remains the driver to beat in the Independents Trophy after tallying his fourth win of the season at Thruxton (25/26 July) on what was a fast and furious weekend in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship.

Returning to action following the traditional mid-season break, the LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing driver punched in an ultra-consistent performance to extend his advantage at the top of the Indy Drivers’ standings to 23 points.

Arriving at the Hampshire circuit having clocked valuable mileage in his Audi A3 Saloon during a recent test at Pembrey, the 27-year-old wasted no time in hitting the ground running on Saturday as he set the fourth fastest time in practice. 

Come the Qualifying Race later that afternoon, the two-time race winner found himself in the thick of the action as he went wheel-to-wheel with a number of drivers before taking the chequered flag in ninth place. 

Starting on the fifth row of the grid for the first of Sunday’s three races around the 2.36-mile circuit, the former Jack Sears Trophy winner went on to wow the crowds with a captivating battle with the Restart Racing Hyundai i30 N of James Dorlin. 

Getting the better of Dorlin in the opening exchanges, Doble then covered him off in the remaining laps with a wheel-perfect display that crucially secured him a fourth Independent win of the season. 

With the field so tightly bunched together, Doble spent the remaining two races in the midst of the midfield battle, clinching a brace of top tens. Crucially, these translated into second and fourth place finishes when it came to the Independents Trophy. 

In addition to extending his own lead in the Independents Drivers’ Championship over the course of the weekend, Doble also ensured that LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing remain out front in the Independents Teams’ too. 

Mikey Doble: “It’s been one of those weekend’s where we’ve ticked all the boxes in terms of scoring an Independent win and extending our lead in the championship, yet I’m leaving having wanted a little more.

“We had a really good two-day test at Pembrey and the work that we carried out there left me feeling pretty confident that we could win some races this weekend. Sadly that didn’t materialise as we didn’t quite have the balance we wanted in the car. 

“Saturday was strong, and that set us up for a solid Sunday where we chipped away. Getting that Independents win in race one was a great way to start the day and we then just tried to keep our nose clean and make as much progress as possible in the remaining two races.

“Obviously I’d have liked a little more results-wise but to come away having stretched our lead is something we can’t turn our nose up at. I’m unsure how we’ll fare at Knockhill but I know the team will pull out all the stops to ensure we have as strong a car as possible.”

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season continues in less than two weeks as the series makes its annual trip north of the border to Knockhill (8/9 August).

title.rendered: Huge crowd enjoys high-speed BTCC action at Thruxton
